 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.54,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 21-11-2023 at about 8.30 p.m., the petitioner was a pillion rider on the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-HP- 0560, the same being ridden by its rider slowly,
cautiously, by observing all the traffic rules, on the Sarjapura road.

When they reached near Chandra Mowleshwara Temple, Sarjapura Village, Anekal Taluk, the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-Z-8007, drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner from opposite direction.
Due to said impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Town Hospital, Sarjapura, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident she was working as cleaning staff at R.K.T. Catering, Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.18,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The Sarjapura Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.54,00,000/-, with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has denied the alleged accident and involvement of the alleged car in the alleged accident.

It has contended that, the petition against the respondents herein is bad for mis-joinder or unnecessary and non-joinder of necessary parties, as the respondents herein are unnecessarily made as parties with ulterior motive to claim compensation.

Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay any Uppara Pushpa Alias Pushpa vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71916792/
2 compensation in the above case.

sentences.text: Further it is contended that, the car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-Z-8007 had not at all involved in the alleged accident.
The jurisdictional police without conducting proper investigation have filed the false charge-sheet against the driver of said car, in collusion with the petitioner.
However, as there are contradictory claims and there are variance in information given to the hospital authority and police authority by the petitioner about the alleged accident.

Further it is contended that, there is total negligence on the part of the petitioner/rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-51- HP-0560, as he was riding his motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the insured car.
However, the facts have been twisted and given wrong description and a false charge-sheet has been filed against the driver of the said car.
Further it is contended that, the petitioner has not made the owner/insurer of motorcycle bearing No.KA-51-HP-0560 as a party to the present claim petition.
As such, the claim petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-Z-8007, in favour of respondent No.2 and the liability of this respondent, subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further it is contended that, the driver of the car bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-Z-8007 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the same and was disqualified to drive the said vehicle at the time of the alleged accident.

But, the insured/owner of said vehicle has knowingly allowed the said driver to drive the same, without holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said class of vehicle at the time of alleged accident and thereby he has committed breach of contract of insurance.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by her.

Further it is contended that, at the time of alleged accident the petitioner was riding a two-wheeler without wearing any protective head gear/helmet and hence there is a violation of provisions of Section 129 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the petitioner has not made the driver of the car as a party to the proceedings.
In fact, the driver of the said vehicle was also proper and necessary party for the adjudication of claim petition.

Further it is contended that,
the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.

For the above denials and contentions,
it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 21-11-2023 at about 8.30 p.m., near Chandra Mowleshwara Temple, Sarjapura Village, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-Z-8007 ?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?

At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.1 in respect of car bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-Z-8007 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondents No.2, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.1 has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-51-HP-0560 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-Z-8007.
But, the respondent No.1 has failed to establish the said contentions.

Except examining the Medical Record Incharge of Town Hospital, Bengaluru, as R.W.1, the respondent No.1 has neither adduced any evidence, nor produced any document to show that, at the relevant point of time of accident the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-51-HP-0560 was riding the same in rash and negligent manner and due to his self negligence the accident in question has taken place.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-Z-8007 and dashing the same to motorcycle of the petitioner from opposite direction.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length

, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-51-HP-0560 or there was any contributory negligence on his part, in the cause of accident.

13. Further, the Ex.P.4 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of 30 feet wide road, near Chandra Mowleshwara Temple, Sarjapura Village, Anekal Taluk, in between the offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-Z-8007 and oncoming motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-HP-0560.
Further, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-HP-0560, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.11 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-Z-8007 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-Z-8007.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

She has suffered T-12 fracture with paraplegia T- 10 - L-2 spine fixation bi-lateral pubic rami fracture.

The P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner has sustained above injuries in the road traffic accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth, which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the above medical records of the petitioner.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 21-11-2023 at about 8.30 p.m., near Chandra Mowleshwara Temple, Sarjapura Village, Anekal Taluk, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA- 51-Z-8007.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-Z-8007 and she has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, she has sustained T-12 fracture with paraplegia T-10 - L-2 spine fixation bi-lateral pubic rami fracture.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment,
attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages,
such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
19. Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove her age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of her Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.12.
As per Ex.P.12, the date of birth of the petitioner is 01-01-1984.

sentences.text: This clearly goes to show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 40 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered T-12 fracture with paraplegia T-10 - L-2 spine fixation bi-lateral pubic rami fracture and for the said injuries the petitioner has undergone surgery.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 60% to the whole body.

The Ex.P.10 wound certificate, Ex.P.13 discharge summary, Ex.P.15 clinical note and Ex.P.16 x-ray also clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and for the said injuries she has undergone surgery.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
He has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

Further it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 21-11-2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 08-09-2025, which is after lapse of one year and nine months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further he has admitted that, the petitioner has not undergone any surgery with respect of lower limb, the petitioner does not require further treatment in respect of lower limb, there is no fracture at lower limb, the petitioner has not undergone any surgery for pubic ramus fracture, he has not assessed disability with respect of pubic ramus fracture, the petitioner does not require removal of implants, the petitioner is not under any active medical treatment, but he is undergoing physiotherapy, he has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability and the GCS level of petitioner is normal.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the physical disability of 40% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 40% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
20. The petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, before accident she was working as cleaning staff at R.K.T. Catering, Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.18,000/- per month.
Further, she has deposed that, due to the accidental injuries she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The respondent No.1 has specifically denied the same.

In such circumstances,
the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
She has not produced any document to show that, before accident she was working as cleaning staff at R.K.T. Catering, Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.18,000/- per month.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2023.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered at Rs.16,000/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner at Rs.1,92,000/-.

21. As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 40 years is 15.

Therefore, taking into consideration the injury sustained and the disability suffered by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.80,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.

is awarded towards the attendant charges.
25. Food and nourishment:

26. Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of B.C. Colony, Obaganipalli,
Thimmapuram, Kambadur, Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh, the accident has taken place near Chandra Mowleshwara Temple, Sarjapura Village, Anekal Taluk and she has taken treatment at Kumar Hospital, Anantapuram.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places

,
compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.

The petitioner has taken treatment for 8 days as in-patient at Kumar Hospital, Anantapuram, for the grievous injuries sustained by her.
She might have taken rest for about 3 months and lost her income for the said period.
Therefore, Rs.16,000 x 3 = Rs.48,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
28. Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 40 years and unfortunately she has sustained T-12 fracture with paraplegia T-10 - L-2 spine fixation bi-lateral pubic rami fracture.
The evidence shows that, she has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 40% to the whole body.

Therefore, awarding Uppara Pushpa Alias Pushpa vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71916792/
8 compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.

The P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the petitioner does not require removal of implants.
Further, nowhere in the evidence the P.W.2 has stated that, the petitioner is in need of any further treatment.
In such circumstances, question of awarding compensation to the petitioner towards future medical expenses does not arise.

1. Loss of future income Rs. 11,52,000-00 2.

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,00,448/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
31. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-51-Z-8007.

Further, as per the true copy of reply given by the owner of offending vehicle, to the notice issued by the investigation officer under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is marked as Ex.P.7, the driver of offending vehicle by name Yesanulla S/o Noor Mohammed was holding valid and effective driving licence bearing No.KA-05-19990000979 to drive the said vehicle and it is valid from 22-04-1999 to 19- 03-2030.
The policy issued by the respondent No.1 bearing No.MW046110, in respect of offending car, was valid from 31-08-2023 to 30-08-2024.
As such, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1 in respect of offending vehicle was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 21-11-2023.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-Z-8007 the accident in question has taken place.

In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage Uppara Pushpa Alias Pushpa vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71916792/
9 caused by the said vehicle.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,00,448/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.1, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
